title: Cap. X Arg. VII→VIII open: if reprobation only from antecedent unbelief, all infants dying before free will—even pagans—must be elect and saved
pass_a_gloss: Reprobation having been laid down as only from antecedent unbelief and actual contempt or neglect of Divine grace, it is necessary that we lay down as certain by catholic faith that all infants, even of Pagans, who die before the use of free will, are elect and will be safe. The reason is at hand, Because such could not yet contract the guilt of unbelief from contempt of the Gospel and of Divine grace.
pass_b_english: Grant reprobation only from antecedent unbelief plus actual contempt or neglect of divine grace, and catholic faith would have to treat as certain that every infant who dies before free will—even a pagan’s—is elect and will be saved. Why? Such a child could not yet incur unbelief’s guilt from scorning the Gospel and divine grace.
source_text: Posita reprobatione non nisi ex antecedente infidelitate et contemtu actuali sive neglectu gratiae Divinae, necesse est ut ponamus tanquam certum fide catholica, omnes infantes, etiam Paganorum, qui moriuntur ante usum liberi arbitrii, electos esse et salvos fore. Ratio in promptu est, Quia tales infidelitatis reatum ex contemptu Evangelii et gratiae Divinae contrahere nondum potuerunt.
